decisions.decision: 'The fabric' in Phase 24 criterion 8 is read NARROWLY
decisions.rationale: A fabric this repo can be deployed and operated as, with an admission posture stated on every relay-capable door — not the default argv. The wider reading would have returned 24 to PARTIAL and 19 with it, at a cost of 19+3 argv sites made refuse-to-start. Owner declined it.

decisions.decision: Compile elfconv ITSELF to wasm; do NOT make RISC-V a lift source
decisions.rationale: Remill has zero RISC-V support (grep -ri riscv over the vendored tree returns nothing) and its Sleigh backend vendors no .slaspec. RV64GC semantics would be written from scratch. A wasm-hosted translator reaches RISC-V hosts without that.

decisions.decision: Every LLVM 16->17 change must be compatible in BOTH directions, never replaced outright
decisions.rationale: The native build still runs on LLVM 16 and is the path that currently works. An unconditional llvm/IR/AttributeMask.h include broke it — that header does not exist in 16.

decisions.decision: Link-test BEFORE porting the ELF loader
decisions.rationale: One build attempt priced the LLVM 16->17 skew, the target-library question and the missing-dependency set at once. Had the skew been severe, a 620-line loader port would have been wasted.

decisions.decision: The disclosure gate exempts submodules, derived from git's index (160000 gitlinks), never a path literal
decisions.rationale: elfconv ships .github/workflows and DEMO-04 forbids any workflow file. A hand-maintained list is the population defect this repo has hit four times. The unmeasured part — that GitHub never runs a submodule's workflows — is named as unmeasured in the code.

decisions.decision: Reject a WASIX shim in the executor unless explicitly argued
decisions.rationale: It would hand guest code fork/exec and sockets — the sandbox surface Phases 13.1 and 24 spent their effort narrowing. Not to be widened for a demo.

context_notes: Approach that worked all session: measure before committing to a direction, and treat a document's claim about the code as a hypothesis. Three recorded claims turned out false when checked — elfconv's README on x86 support, the praxis review on verifyChain's depth bound, and my own first draft of a test comment. The AArch64 byte-identical-bitcode check (sha256 ec2dc6f9..., 900 functions) is the regression harness for all elfconv work and it is cheap; run it before believing any elfconv change is safe. Note it FAILED TO FAIL once this session — see the blocking anti-pattern in .continue-here.md.
